title: Output size of the stock 4K size class: 3840x2160 to 3840x2560, in the coprocessor's movie size table (RAM) (A1 II 4.00 port)
artifact: cpapp-b.bin, RAM only: these bytes are not in the file
status: addresses from emulating and reading the A1 II's own code; never read or written on an A1 II. The same word change (outsz2560_v1) works on the A7 IV (requests 26 to 29, F688, F698, F700)
table: movie size table 0x1938488 (base 0x1938404 + 0x84; 0x501834 fills it; the reader 0x5214fe, case 3, loads base + 0xcc = 0x19384d0)

goes_with: the A1 II encoder-side design (3840 x 2560)

sites.note: the second 3840x2160 entry (output width and height; class 4 of the A1 II's table as the emulator counts it, the A7 IV's class 3) [A7 IV 0x143c7bc, A7C II 0x1a531c8, FX2 0x18f60f8]

guards.note: the entry before: 3840, 2160, memory id 0x43e [A7 IV 0x143c7b4, FX2 0x18f60f0]
this entry's memory id, 0x2d9 [A7 IV 0x143c7c0, FX2 0x18f60fc]

precondition: none of its own: the table is read when a movie request is set up; write it with the camera in stills, as on the A7 IV
restore: write the old word back, or cold boot (the set-up fills the table again at start-up)
checked_against: build/emu_size_table.py a1m2_400 (the A1 II's set-up run alone; entries equal the FX2's)
the tbh switches of the A1 II (0x5214fe) and FX2 (0x51fca6) readers, decoded from the files: cases 0 to 5 pick the same entries
the A1 II's DmmCfg.bin: id 0x2d9 = 11 x 13,271,040 bytes
not_shown: the A1 II's format code in 4K (2 on the A7 IV camera, request 25; at code 3 a 3840x2560 picture would need 14,745,600 bytes, more than the 13,271,040-byte unit)
what the settings block 0x19acc14 holds on a camera (the emulation runs the set-up with it zero; the A1 II's head stores 1 where the FX2's stores 0 at 0x501894, before the entries)
